paragraphs: There were two: one in Shmuel's time, as in Pesachim 40a, where Shmuel issued a practical ruling in the village of the household of bar Chasho; and Yimar bar Chasho, in Rava's time, as in Ketubot 84b.[^1][^2]

notes.text: כפסחים: followed on next line by מ. is contextually Pesachim 40a: the displaced numeral belongs to the locator rather than an unexplained personal abbreviation. The prior colon after tractate is unusual; neither punctuation nor modern page is newly verified. פד: gives Ketubot 84b conventionally.

עבד עובדא is issued a practical ruling. The parenthetical בכפר supplies village, while דבי בר חשו is the household-of-bar-Chasho phrase; the precise village/house relation remains compressed. Hyman distinguishes two periods/attestations, first Shmuel then Yimar in Rava’s time; no single-person/shared-father identity is inferred. All names are untitled, with Rava a name, not a Rav prefix. Machine ימר versus supplied יימר remains provenance.
